hero.headline: Disassemble. Understand. Conquer.
hero.description: A deep-dive reverse engineering competition. Peel back layers of obfuscation, trace execution paths, and extract flags hidden in binaries, firmware, and protocols.

faq.a: Primarily x86/x64, but expect ARM, MIPS, and custom VMs in higher-difficulty challenges.
Ghidra, IDA Free, Binary Ninja, Radare2, x64dbg/GDB, pwndbg, and Frida are all commonly used. The lab VM has these pre-installed.
No. All malware samples are defanged — network callbacks are redirected and destructive payloads are neutered. Still, work inside the provided sandbox VM.
Flags are in RE{...} format and are embedded within the binary or revealed upon successful analysis.

lab.title: RE Challenges
lab.subtitle: Binaries and firmware targets
lab.description: Analyze the provided targets and extract the hidden flag from each. Work inside the lab VM — do not run unknown binaries on your host machine. Flags are in RE{...} format.

questions.title: intro_x64
questions.description: A stripped ELF x64 binary. It accepts a string argument and prints 'Correct!' if the input matches the expected value. Find the expected string and submit the flag.
questions.hint: Open in Ghidra. Find main(), follow the string comparison, and read off the expected bytes.

questions.title: vm_check
questions.description: A Windows PE that implements a small custom bytecode VM to verify a password. Reconstruct the VM opcodes and determine the correct password.
questions.hint: Look for a dispatch loop — a switch or jump table indexed by the opcode byte.

questions.title: router_fw.bin
questions.description: A firmware image from a consumer router. Extract the filesystem, find the hidden flag file, and determine the credentials used to protect it.
questions.hint: Use binwalk to extract the firmware. The flag is not in plaintext — check config files and compiled binaries inside.

questions.title: mystery.pcap + decoder
questions.description: A packet capture file and an unknown binary that speaks the same protocol. Reverse the binary's protocol handler and decode the flag transmitted in the capture.

allowed: Use any RE tool — Ghidra, IDA, Binary Ninja, x64dbg, GDB, Frida, etc.
Run provided binaries inside the lab VM only
Use dynamic analysis, tracing, and hooking on lab targets
Search online for general techniques, documentation, and writeups on similar challenges
Collaborate with your registered team members
not_allowed: Run any lab binary outside the provided sandbox VM
Share flags or full solutions with other teams during the event
Exfiltrate any lab files outside the competition environment
Attempt to attack competition infrastructure or other participants' lab instances
